walkthroughs.body_html:
Particles & Radiation — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Particles & Radiation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Particles & Radiation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A car travels 4 km north then 3 km east. What is its displacement magnitude?
options: 7 km
5 km
1 km
25 km

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
options: Acceleration
Momentum
Kinetic energy
Weight

mcqs.q: Which type of nuclear radiation is most ionising?
options: Yes — only infrared and radio waves are non-ionising.
Alpha radiation — large, doubly charged particles cause the most ionisation per unit distance.
Beta radiation is most ionising because it consists of fast electrons.
Gamma is most ionising because it can travel furthest and pass through almost anything.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a fundamental particle: proton, electron, or neutron?
options: Only the electron — protons and neutrons are made of quarks.
Yes — only infrared and radio waves are non-ionising.
Only the proton is fundamental; electrons and neutrons are composite.
All three (proton, electron, neutron) are fundamental particles that cannot be broken down.
No — its photon energy is below the threshold required to ionise atoms; ionising radiation includes UV (high energy), X-rays and gamma.
Yes — all electromagnetic radiation is ionising because it carries energy.
Beta radiation is most ionising because it consists of fast electrons.
Yes — only infrared and radio waves are non-ionising.
